note: Sat 28 Nov 2026 SGT weekend catch-up run. The last run restamped Wed 25 Nov's close because Thu 26 Nov (Thanksgiving) was shut and Fri's half-day hadn't opened; that session has now happened and it moved the tape hard. Fri 27 Nov half-day US close: S&P +1.60% to 7297.49, Nasdaq +2.31% to 24129.50, Dow +1.18%, Russell +1.71%, VIX -11.16% to 23.81 -- still elevated, but a sharp reversal off Wednesday's close. The SAME day, precious metals/miners exploded: SLV +6.20% to $39.40, GLD +2.12% to $334.40, gold futures +3.75% to $3668.50, GDX +7.16%, SILJ +8.79%, SLVP +7.82%, AG +9.80%, PAAS +7.43%, HL +7.45%. HK tech also surged on a separate but coincident catalyst: SMIC (0981.HK) +16.39%, part of a record +17.6% one-day move in China's CSI Semiconductor index after Beijing's State Council 'national team'/Central Huijin stabilization pledge (Tencent +3.23%, Xiaomi +4.51%). Causation matters here: Wed 25 Nov's actual prints came in HOT, not dovish -- core PCE +0.3% m/m/+3.3% y/y, Q3 GDP revised UP to +4.3% (vs 3.5% consensus), jobless claims fell to 189K (vs 201K forecast) -- and the Fed remains in a hiking cycle (3.75-4.00% target, hiked Sept/Oct 2026), with prediction markets pricing ~90-97% odds of another 25bp hike at the Dec 8-9 FOMC. The 10Y (~4.93-4.94%) and DXY (~104.0) both ROSE Friday, so the metals move was NOT a falling-rates/weak-dollar trade -- it is best read as a technically-driven short-covering bounce off an extreme oversold setup (silver had hit a 15-month low days earlier), riding the same risk-on wave as the China-stimulus-driven chip rally rather than a dovish pivot. Asian cash markets are closed for the weekend; HK/SG settled Fri 27 Nov, JP/KR's Fri bar had not yet consolidated at run time (lag, not a holiday) so JP/KR calls still reference Thu 26 Nov. Regime recalibrated from the prior restamp given the hot data reinforces hikes (not cuts) while the equity/metals bounce itself is read as technical, not a risk-appetite reversal -- riskOnProb and byAssetClass tilts adjusted modestly for the Friday price action without overreading a single holiday-thinned session. All 40 universe calls plus the 9-name rare-earth basket were re-reviewed; GLD, SLV, GDX-adjacent commodity calls, SPY/QQQ/IWM and BTC-USD got the most substantive driver refreshes for the Friday session; names with no direct new catalyst keep their Thu/Wed-anchored driver language reconfirmed.

macro.regime: Hawkish-Fed, overheating economy -- equity/metals bounce is technical (oversold short-covering + China stimulus), not a risk-appetite or rate-cut regime change
macro.narrative: Fri 27 Nov's half-day US session reversed hard off Wednesday's air-pocket close: S&P +1.60% to 7297.49, Nasdaq +2.31%, VIX -11.16% to 23.81 (still above pre-crash norms). The hot Wed 25 Nov data cluster that triggered the prior selloff -- core PCE +0.3% m/m/+3.3% y/y, Q3 GDP revised up to +4.3% (vs 3.5% consensus), jobless claims down to 189K (vs 201K forecast) -- did NOT reverse; if anything it hardens the case for a Dec 9 hike, with Kalshi/Polymarket pricing ~90-97% odds and Fed's Waller floating a jumbo 50bp move while Williams won't rule out consecutive hikes. The 10Y (~4.93-4.94%) and DXY (~104.0) both rose Friday, confirming the equity/metals rally was not rates-driven. Instead, two separate catalysts landed the same day: (1) China's State Council 'national team'/Central Huijin stabilization pledge triggered a record +17.6% one-day move in the CSI Semiconductor index, with SMIC (0981.HK) +16.39% and Hua Hong +~20.7% the standouts -- a sector re-rating of 'chip-sovereignty' plays, not an SMIC-idiosyncratic event, lifting Tencent/Xiaomi and the broader HK tech book too; and (2) gold/silver/miners staged a mechanical short-covering bounce off an extreme oversold setup (silver had touched a 15-month low days earlier) that happened to ride the same risk-on wave -- SLV +6.20%, GDX +7.16%, SILJ +8.79%, gold futures +3.75% -- rather than any dovish-Fed or weak-dollar trigger. China separately extended its gallium/germanium/antimony export-curb suspension on the US through 27 Jan 2027, a shorter (61-day) extension than last year's full year, keeping it as live leverage rather than a resolved truce. Net: this is a genuine, broad relief bounce (NYSE advancers led decliners ~3.25:1 Friday) sitting on top of an unresolved hawkish-Fed/overheating-economy backdrop and a still-fragile, policy-dependent China-chip rally -- constructive for the levered-silver margin math and the HK-tech sleeve near-term, but not a regime change until it survives a full week past the holiday-thinned print and the Dec 9 FOMC.
